content: If you are allergic to conjugated estrogens or bazedoxifene, or if you have any other allergies, inform your doctor or pharmacist before taking this medication. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could trigger allergic reactions or other complications. Avoid smoking or using tobacco products while on this medication. Notify your doctor if you have recently undergone surgery, are planning to have surgery, or if you will be immobile for an extended period (e.g., during a long plane flight). Prolonged immobility increases the risk of blood clots, particularly if you are taking an estrogen-containing product. This medication may cause blotchy, dark areas on your face and skin, a condition known as melasma. Sunlight can exacerbate this effect, so limit your exposure to the sun, avoid tanning booths and sunlamps, and use sunscreen or protective clothing when outdoors. If you are nearsighted or wear contact lenses, you may experience vision problems or difficulty wearing your lenses while taking this medication. This medication must not be used during pregnancy. Estrogens can pass into breast milk and may reduce both the quality and quantity of milk produced. It is unknown whether bazedoxifene passes into breast milk. Breastfeeding is not recommended while using this medication. Drug interactions may alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal supplements, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication may interfere with certain laboratory tests (e.g., metyrapone test, blood clotting tests, thyroid tests), potentially leading to inaccurate results. In the event of an overdose, if the individual has severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call emergency services immediately (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Regular physical exams, including laboratory and medical tests (e.g., blood pressure checks, breast exams/mammograms, pelvic exams, Pap smears), should be conducted while taking this medication. Follow your doctor’s instructions for self-examining your breasts and report any lumps immediately. Keep all medical and laboratory appointments. To reduce the risk of heart disease and stroke, manage high blood pressure, high cholesterol, and diabetes. Lifestyle changes such as reducing stress, eating a low-fat/low-salt diet, losing weight if overweight, exercising regularly, and quitting smoking can help control or prevent these conditions. Engage in mental exercises (e.g., reading, solving crossword puzzles) to help prevent dementia. To promote healthy bones, increase weight-bearing exercise, quit smoking, limit alcohol consumption, and eat a well-balanced diet rich in calcium and vitamin D. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication in its original packaging at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Once the foil pouch is opened, the U.S. product expires after 60 days, and the Canadian product expires after 45 days. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs.
